hook.en: Most compounds of sodium are white, but transition-metal compounds come in every colour, many are attracted by a magnet, and many speed up industrial reactions. All three come from unpaired d electrons.
hook.kn: ಸೋಡಿಯಂ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು ಬಹುತೇಕ ಬಿಳಿ, ಆದರೆ ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣ ಲೋಹದ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು ಬಣ್ಣಬಣ್ಣದವು, ಕಾಂತಕ್ಕೆ ಆಕರ್ಷಿತವಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕೈಗಾರಿಕಾ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳನ್ನು ವೇಗಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಇವೆಲ್ಲಕ್ಕೂ ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗದ d ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳು ಕಾರಣ.

objectives.en: Explain the colour of transition-metal ions
Describe catalytic behaviour, interstitial compounds and alloys

narration.en: Most compounds of sodium are white, but transition-metal compounds come in every colour, many are attracted by a magnet, and many speed up industrial reactions. All three come from unpaired d electrons.
narration.kn: ಸೋಡಿಯಂ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು ಬಹುತೇಕ ಬಿಳಿ, ಆದರೆ ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣ ಲೋಹದ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು ಬಣ್ಣಬಣ್ಣದವು, ಕಾಂತಕ್ಕೆ ಆಕರ್ಷಿತವಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕೈಗಾರಿಕಾ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳನ್ನು ವೇಗಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಇವೆಲ್ಲಕ್ಕೂ ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗದ d ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳು ಕಾರಣ.

body.en: A substance with unpaired electrons is paramagnetic: it is attracted into a magnetic field. One with all electrons paired is diamagnetic. For 3d ions the moment comes almost entirely from electron spin, so the spin-only formula gives it from the number of unpaired electrons, n. The unit is the Bohr magneton (BM).
body.kn: ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗದ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳಿರುವ ವಸ್ತು ಅನುಕಾಂತೀಯ; ಎಲ್ಲ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳು ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗಿದ್ದರೆ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಂತೀಯ. ಸ್ಪಿನ್-ಮಾತ್ರ ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಭ್ರಾಮಕ μ = √(n(n+2)) BM.

title.en: On the board: magnetism and colour

say.en: Unpaired electrons make an ion paramagnetic. The spin-only moment is root n into n plus 2 Bohr magnetons.
One unpaired electron gives 1.73, three give 3.87, five give 5.92. Iron two plus, d six, has four unpaired: 4.90.
In a complex the d orbitals split. An electron jumps up by absorbing one colour of light; we see the complementary colour.
Ti three plus, d one, is purple; Cu two plus, d nine, is blue. d zero and d ten ions have no d–d jump, so they are colourless.
Transition metals are good catalysts because of variable oxidation states and large surfaces. Similar radii let them form alloys.
Small atoms such as carbon, nitrogen and hydrogen fit into the metal lattice: interstitial compounds, hard and high-melting.

title.en: Colour, catalysis, interstitial compounds and alloys

body.en: In a complex or a hydrated ion, the d orbitals split into two energy levels. An electron absorbs visible light to jump to the upper level (a d–d transition), and we see the complementary colour: [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is violet, [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ blue. d⁰ and d¹⁰ ions (Sc³⁺, Ti⁴⁺, Zn²⁺, Cu⁺) are colourless. Transition metals are good catalysts because they show variable oxidation states and offer surfaces for adsorption: V₂O₅ (Contact process), Fe (Haber process), Ni (hydrogenation); Fe³⁺ catalyses the reaction of I⁻ with S₂O₈²⁻. Small atoms such as H, C and N fit into their lattices to give hard, high-melting, inert interstitial compounds. Similar atomic radii let them form alloys: brass (Cu–Zn), bronze (Cu–Sn), steels.
body.kn: d–d ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣದಿಂದ ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣ ಲೋಹ ಅಯಾನುಗಳು ಬಣ್ಣ ಹೊಂದಿವೆ; d⁰ ಮತ್ತು d¹⁰ ಅಯಾನುಗಳು ಬಣ್ಣರಹಿತ. ಬದಲಾಗುವ ಆಕ್ಸಿಡೀಕರಣ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಗಳಿಂದ ಅವು ಉತ್ತಮ ವೇಗವರ್ಧಕಗಳು. ಅವು ಅಂತರಾಳೀಯ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಮಿಶ್ರಲೋಹಗಳನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

Cu²⁺ is d⁹: one unpaired electron, 1.73 BM.

narration.en: Spin-only magnetic moment against the number of unpaired electrons. Mn²⁺ and Fe³⁺ are both d⁵: set n = 5 (5.92 BM). Cu²⁺ is d⁹: one unpaired electron, 1.73 BM. Zn²⁺ (d¹⁰): n = 0, diamagnetic.

problem.en: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Fe²⁺ (Z of Fe = 26).

steps.en: Fe²⁺ = [Ar] 3d⁶: five d orbitals hold 6 electrons, so one pair and 4 unpaired electrons: n = 4.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Fe²⁺ (Z of Fe = 26).

problem.en: A divalent 3d ion has a spin-only moment of 3.87 BM. How many unpaired electrons does it have, and which ion could it be?

steps.en: A d³ ion with charge +2: V²⁺ (V is 3d³ 4s², so V²⁺ is 3d³). (A d⁷ ion such as Co²⁺, high spin, also has 3 unpaired electrons.)
